newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February index of leading indicators rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February index of leading indicators rise.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle, rose for the sixth consecutive month in February, a cabinet agency said on Thursday.
The index rose 0.8 percent in February from January, marking the highest level since June of 1995, the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said in a statement.
But the index of coincident indicators dropped in February, losing 0.7 percent to 102.0 from a month ago.
The council said the economy remained in a "green light" condition, indicating a possible recovery, for the fourth straight month.
"Overall, the domestic economy hasn't entered an overall recovery, and the recovering pace is still slow," the council said.
Thirty-one percent of a sample polling of manufacturing executives said the economy would improve after three months, up from 20 percent in January, the council said.
The percentage of executives who said the economy would deteriorate dropped to 13 percent in February from 14 percent in January.
The rest said the economy would remain unchanged.
